extracted.intended_audience: historians and scholars of maritime exploration; readers of scholarly edited voyage narratives (Hakluyt Society membership and similar audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or using a scholarly edited translation of early modern voyage narratives (here: the voyages of Pedro Fernandez de Quiros), including selection of sources, editorial division, appendices, maps, and critical commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the best and most detailed narrative as principal source
rubrics_metrics.description: The best and most detailed narrative of both voyages is contained in a work which remained in manuscript until twenty-eight years ago, when it was edited and published at Madrid by Don Justo Zaragoza. It is entitled History of the Discovery of the Austrial Regions, made by the General Pedro Fernandez de Quiros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on Zaragoza’s Historia as the principal text for translation/edition when it is the fullest surviving account; identify and state which manuscript/edition is being used as the base text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multiple contemporaneous narratives for completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: For the voyage of Quiros in 1606 there are no less than four separate accounts: (1) the Historia by Belmonte Bermudez, (2) a narrative/log by Gaspar Gonzalez de Leza, (3) the account in Torquemada’s Monarquia Indiana, and (4) a letter from Luis Vaez de Torres to the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print or summarise all substantive contemporary accounts (narratives, logs, official letters) so readers can compare perspectives and corroborate events; explain the particular interest or value of each (e.g., Leza = log with daily courses; Torquemada = polished account; Torres = letter with post-separation events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide lengthy manuscript narratives into convenient parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Historia, as published by Zaragoza, is continuous in eighty-one chapters. It has been found more convenient to divide the translation into two parts: the first containing the second voyage of Mendaña, and the second part being the story of the voyage of Quiros in 1606.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a continuous manuscript is long, split the translation into logical parts (by voyage, by expedition, or by major narrative units) to aid readability and reference; state the division explicitly in the introduction and table of contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint short related reports to make the monograph complete
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a short report of the second voyage of Mendaña, to Antonio de Morga, the Governor of the Philippines, by Quiros himself. I have caused it to be reprinted in this volume, in order to make the monograph of Quiros complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include shorter contemporary reports (even if previously published elsewhere) when they materially complete the documentary picture of the voyage; explicitly state why each supplementary document is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide maps and reproduce original legends and charts
rubrics_metrics.description: MAPS: Planos de las Bahías..., New Hebrides, Banks and Duff Groups..., Routes of Mendaña, 1595; Quiros, 1606, and Torres, 1606. Legends on the Four Maps signed by Diego de Prado y Tobar. In Pocket at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include facsimile maps (with legends reproduced), route-plots, and place them conveniently (pocket at end or plates) so readers can consult geographic evidence used in the text; reproduce long original map-titles/legends separately when informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appendices of memorials, letters, and documentary material
rubrics_metrics.description: APPENDIX includes: Eighth Memorial of Quiros; Memorials of Quiros 1607, 1609; Memorials touching Papers printed by Quiros; Letters from Diego de Prado y Tobar, 1613; Note on the Memorials of Quiros by the Council of the Indies, 1610; Memorial touching Papers printed by Quiros, 1610; Memorial by Juan Luis Arias, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and print key memorials, letters, and administrative documents in an appendix to allow readers to judge the navigator’s representations and the governmental response; select representative specimens when documents are numerous and repetitive (the editor here chose three memorials as specimens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss authorship, editorial responsibility, and textual interpolations
rubrics_metrics.description: The narratives were evidently dictated by Quiros, or written from his notes; but Señor Zaragoza gives reasons for the belief that the work, in its present form, was written by Luis de Belmonte Bermudez, a young man who was Secretary to Quiros during the voyage of 1606, and that it contains several passages for which the Secretary was alone responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and state authorship questions in the introduction, point out poetic or stylistic passages attributable to a secretary or interpolator, and explain editorial choices made in light of authorship doubts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use navigational data to identify geographic locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The latitudes recorded by Quiros, Torres, and Leza, and the courses and distances run, enable us to identify the islands discovered by Quiros in crossing the Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference narrative descriptions with recorded latitudes, courses, distances, and contemporary charts to propose identifications of islands/places; cite authorities (e.g., Sir William Wharton) when making identifications and explain reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit inferior or redundant versions when unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: In the work entitled Hechos del Marques de Cañete... Book VI contains an abbreviated version of the narrative in the Historia... For these reasons I have considered it unnecessary to translate the version of Suarez de Figueroa, as it is merely a mutilated version of the narrative in the Historia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reproduce versions that are mere abridgements or corruptions of the principal text unless they add substantive new information; justify omissions in the introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide scholarly apparatus: introduction, bibliography, index, corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents include Dedication, Introduction, Note on the Cartography..., Bibliography, With British Museum Press-marks, Index, Maps, Appendix. Corrections have been applied to the text (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a full scholarly apparatus: a critical introduction discussing context and editorial practice, bibliography and museum references, an index, list of emendations/corrections, and colophon so the edition is usable for researchers.
